name: Layered Garden Vegetable Terrine with Pea Puree, Glazed Roots and Parmesan Tuile
description: An elegant vegetarian course, pairing zucchini, peas, and other delicious vegetables.
headnote: Slicing the vegetables paper-thin and layering them into a terrine turns a simple vegetable side into something with actual cross-section — every slice reveals the same striping of colors. The parmesan tuile is there for contrast as much as flavor: everything else on the plate is soft, puréed, or glazed, so the one crisp element carries more weight than its size suggests.

steps.instruction: Prepare the Vegetable Terrine
Make the Pea Purée
Glaze the Vegetables
Make the Parmesan Tuile
(Optional) Foam Element.
Plate Like a Michelin Chef.
Lightly brush all sliced vegetables with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Grill or roast slices briefly (just until tender but still structured).
Line a small ring mold or ramekin with zucchini slices.
Layer vegetables in a repeating pattern (zucchini → beet → squash → carrot).
Press gently and chill in the fridge for at least 30–60 minutes to set.
Blanch peas in boiling salted water (2–3 minutes), then transfer to ice water.
Blend peas with butter, cream, salt, and a splash of lemon juice until smooth.
Pass through a fine sieve for ultra-smooth texture
Keep warm.
In a pan, melt butter and add honey.
Add carrots and pearl onions; cook until glossy and tender.
In a separate pan, sauté mushrooms until golden.
Season everything lightly with salt.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Place small piles of grated parmesan on parchment paper.
Bake 5–7 minutes until melted and golden.
Cool and shape if desired (drape over a rolling pin for curves).
Warm a light vegetable broth.
Add a pinch of soy lecithin and blend with an immersion blender to create foam.
Place the terrine neatly in the center of a plate.
Add a quenelle (oval scoop) of pea purée on the side.
Arrange glazed carrots, onions, and mushrooms artistically
Add dots of balsamic glaze and a drizzle of olive oil.
Garnish with microgreens, edible flowers, and tuile crisps.
Finish with foam if using.
